patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — 8x8 and Ooma share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

8x8 and Ooma share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose 8x8 only if your buying job matches “Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24” rather than Ooma's shape. Choose Ooma only if your buying job matches “SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.” rather than 8x8's shape. Workflow advantage: 8x8 leans contact-center, team-communication; Ooma leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — 8x8 and Ooma share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: 8x8 is Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24/user/month annual; CC tiers custom/higher.; Ooma is SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.95 — no annual lock-in..
- Company-size focus: 8x8 (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Ooma (solo, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: 8x8-leaning contact-center, team-communication vs Ooma-leaning —.
- Researched limits: 8x8 — Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Ooma — SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited.

Limitations — 8x8: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Mandatory regulatory/service fees frequently sit on top of list seats; Ooma: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Call queues, CRM and auto-dialer require Pro Plus.

Poor-fit cases: 8x8 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated · Ooma is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited · Avoid 8x8 if you actually need Ooma's motion (SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
